Definition: from G2095 and G2372; in fine spirits, i.e. cheerful:--of good cheer, the more cheerfully.
BiblicalUsage: eúthymos is the word for of good cheer, the more cheerfully. In Acts 27:36, the text says "Then were they all of good cheer."
TheologicalSignificance: I take eúthymos as it stands: of good cheer, the more cheerfully.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
